en.title: Time When All Users First Become Connected
en.description:
A log entry time u v means u and v are connected from that moment on, and connections are transitive. Return the time when all given users first belong to the same connected component; if they can never all be connected, output −1. A single user is already connected before any log entry occurs, and this site defines the output as 0 in that case.

This site has made the standard input and output explicit; any range not given by the source is marked as this site's protocol.
en.input: The first line contains n m, followed by n distinct usernames, then m lines of time u v. The source gives no size bounds; on this site 1≤n≤100000, 0≤m≤200000, usernames are 1..20 ASCII letters, digits or underscores, 0≤time≤10⁹, and every user in the logs exists.
en.explanation: Example 1: at time 3 only a and b are connected; c joins at time 7, so output 7. Example 2: a single user needs no connection, so output 0. Example 3: there are no logs, so the two users can never be connected; output −1.
hints: Sort the logs by time and merge the two endpoints with a union-find in order. Each successful merge decreases the number of components by one; the time when it first reaches 1 is the answer.
